decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits at the core of the firm's announced display focus and has been publicly showcased for years, so management keeps it despite having no recent visibility data.
The pegboard-back shelf display extends the core range the firm committed to, and any softness can be attributed to pandemic-related disruption in retail promotions rather than a flawed product.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a pillar of the one-stop offer, so dropping it would contradict the firm's stated direction and earlier decisions to keep it.
The eighth-pallet display completes the publicly presented pallet-size range and runs on already sunk capacity, so management persists with it.
The media-product display serves a shrinking niche, but management has repeatedly justified it as close to the core offer and blames weak demand on temporary market conditions, so it stays for now.
